topics.label: Lecture Overview and Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes students, introduces cancer evolution as the lecture's focus, and outlines key learning outcomes.

topics.label: Clonal Selection and Multistep Genetic Evolution
topics.groupedBecause: The subtopic explains how sequential genetic mutations provide competitive growth advantages driving Darwinian clonal expansion in tissues.

topics.label: Epigenetic Regulation in Malignant Transformation
topics.groupedBecause: The subtopic explores how non-mutational, transient disruptions to the epigenetic landscape can open chromatin and induce tumorigenic phenotypes.

topics.label: Cell of Origin and Cancer Stem Cell Models
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate how tissue differentiation hierarchies and stemness properties influence tumor initiation and progression.

topics.label: Microenvironmental and Inflammatory Tumor Promoters
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how environmental exposures and chronic inflammation act as critical promotional stimuli enabling mutated cells to expand and transform.

topics.label: Microenvironment Dependency and Therapeutic Targeting
topics.groupedBecause: The subtopic describes how established tumors depend on supportive stroma and discusses how targeting this codependency offers therapeutic avenues.

topics.label: Techniques for Investigating Tumor Evolution and Microenvironments
topics.groupedBecause: The subtopic outlines sequencing and spatial omics technologies used to resolve cellular heterogeneity and microenvironmental interactions in tumors.

topics.label: Synthesis and Conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics integrate the lecture's core concepts regarding the multifactorial nature of cancer evolution and provide concluding remarks.
